gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured performance figure for any candidate. The best available is PassMark's CPU database: the Qualcomm SM6125 in the Eonon UA12S Plus-6G scores a CPU Mark of 2,317 (single thread 885), against 1,065 (single thread 526) for the Rockchip RK3562 that our page lists for the Eonon UA13 Plus. That is about 2.2× the multi-thread score.
standout_why: I compared against the How-To Geek budget head-unit article (Ismar Hrnjicevic, 2026-03-28), which has no measured figures, only prices and a 64 GB spec. I also checked bmwinsights.com's Haudio 10.1 'review' (updated 2026-10-30), which only restates the listing and shows no sign of hands-on testing. technobezz.com's Kissound page returned 403, and I didn't open the T3 or mychooz pages. None of the pages I could read has a boot time, CarPlay connect time, latency, brightness figure or benchmark. My finding is new, but it measures the chip, not the head unit. It also covers only the two Eonon units, whose chips are published. The sub-$90 Haudio and Binize units ChatGPT picked don't name their chip, so the benchmark can't be applied to them.
decides: It doesn't change the 'cheapest' pick. That pick turns on price and on whether wireless CarPlay and Android Auto are confirmed, and no named reviewer measured the $72–$150 units at all. What it does give is a named-source reason for the step up: the $319.99 UA12S Plus-6G's chip scores about 2.2× the UA13 Plus's RK3562 in PassMark multi-thread and about 1.7× in single-thread. Use it as an 'if you want it snappier, pay this much more' line, not as the main pick. Label it a chip benchmark from phones and boards, not a test of the head unit.
